PLAN "12-Week gym-based fat loss & glycaemic control program for a 45yo female with type 2 diabetes (metformin)"
TYPE workout
VISIBILITY public

GOALS
  GOAL primary strength:
    name "fat loss and improved glycaemic control"

PHASES
  PHASE "Phase 1" (4 weeks):
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Initial familiarization & conditioning":
        warmup:
          walking 10 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          squat 3x8..12 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          bench_press 3x8..12 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          bent_over_row 3x8..12 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          lat_pulldown 3x8..12 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
        cooldown:
          chest_stretch 5 minutes
          lat_stretch 5 minutes
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Wednesday training 50m "Conditioning & form":
        warmup:
          jog_in_place 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          goblet_squat 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          dumbbell_press 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          dumbbell_row 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          face_pull 3x15..20 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          walking 5 minutes
          shoulder_stretch 3 minutes
    WEEK 1:
      DAY Friday training 60m "Endurance & technique":
        warmup:
          cycling 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          leg_press 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          incline_press 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          cable_row 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          tricep_pushdown 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          hip_mstretch 5 minutes
  PHASE "Phase 2" (4 weeks):
    WEEK 5:
      DAY Monday training 60m "Progression & volume increase":
        warmup:
          walking 8 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          squat 4x6..10 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          bench_press 4x6..10 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          barbell_row 4x6..10 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          lat_pulldown 4x6..10 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
        cooldown:
          quad_stretch 5 minutes
          upper_back_stretch 5 minutes
    WEEK 5:
      DAY Wednesday training 50m "Conditioning density":
        warmup:
          jump_rope 3 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          goblet_squat 4x10..12 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          dumbbell_press 4x10..12 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          dumbbell_row 4x10..12 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          face_pull 4x15..20 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          walking 5 minutes
    WEEK 5:
      DAY Friday training 60m "Technical work & core":
        warmup:
          cycling 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          hip_thrust 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          cable_curl 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          planks 3x30s rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
          side_plank 3x30s each side rpe 5 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          spinal_twist 5 minutes
  PHASE "Phase 3" (4 weeks):
    WEEK 9:
      DAY Monday training 65m "Glycemic-focused resistance":
        warmup:
          walking 8 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          squat 4x6..8 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          bench_press 4x6..8 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          barbell_row 4x6..8 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          lat_pulldown 4x6..8 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
        cooldown:
          leg_curl 5 minutes
      …
    WEEK 9:
      DAY Wednesday training 55m "Conditioning & mobility":
        warmup:
          rowing 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          leg_press 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          incline_press 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          cable_row 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          tricep_extension 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          mobility routine 8 minutes
    WEEK 9:
      DAY Friday training 60m "Core & stability":
        warmup:
          jog_in_place 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          hip_thrust 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          pulldown_through 3x12..15 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          plank 3x45s rpe 4 rest 60 seconds
          hollow_hold 3x30s rpe 4 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          back_stretch 5 minutes
  PHASE "Phase 4" (4 weeks):
    WEEK 13:
      DAY Monday training 65m "Peak phase setup":
        warmup:
          treadmill_blast 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          squat 5x5 rpe 7 rest 120 seconds
          bench_press 5x5 rpe 7 rest 120 seconds
          barbell_row 5x5 rpe 7 rest 120 seconds
          lat_pulldown 5x5 rpe 7 rest 120 seconds
        cooldown:
          mobility circuit 10 minutes
    WEEK 13:
      DAY Wednesday training 60m "Conditioning blocks":
        warmup:
          cycling 6 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          leg_press 4x12 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          incline_press 4x12 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          cable_row 4x12 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
          bicep_curl 3x12 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          calf_raise 5 minutes
    WEEK 13:
      DAY Friday training 60m "Assessment prep":
        warmup:
          rowing 5 minutes
        main straight_sets:
          deadlift 3x5 rpe 7 rest 120 seconds
          dumbbell_press 3x8..12 rpe 7 rest 90 seconds
          rear_delt_fly 3x12 rpe 7 rest 60 seconds
        cooldown:
          full_body_stretch 8 minutes

NUTRITION GUIDANCE (diabetes-focused, practical, within scope)
  CALORIC TARGET
    - Start with a modest caloric deficit: aim for -500 kcal/day from estimated maintenance.
    - Reassess every 2–3 weeks based on weight change and energy.

  MACRONUTRIENTS
    - Protein: 1.6–2.2 g/kg body weight per day to support lean mass and satiety.
    - Carbohydrates: distribute evenly across meals, focusing on high-fiber sources; target roughly 1.5–2.5 g/kg depending on tolerance and activity.
    - Fat: fill remaining calories with healthy fats; emphasize monounsaturated and omega-3 fats.

  MEAL TIMING & ORDERING
    - Eat regular meals with balanced protein, fiber, and fats to improve glycemic control.
    - Include a protein-rich snack or small meal within 1–2 hours post-workout.
    - Post-exercise carbohydrate window: 0–60 minutes after training, include a moderate carbohydrate portion with protein.

  GLYCEMIC AWARENESS
    - Monitor blood glucose before and after workouts if advised by clinician.
    - If hypoglycemia risk exists, carry fast-acting carbohydrates (glucose tablets) and adjust meals around training.
    - Prefer low-glycemic index (GI) carbohydrate choices most meals; resistant starch and non-starchy vegetables recommended.

  BEHAVIORAL STRATEGIES
    - Consistency over perfection; 4–5 days/week training with 2 rest days as needed.
    - Hydration: 2–3 liters/day unless contraindicated.
    - Sleep: target 7–9 hours per night.

  SUGGESTED DAILY PATTERN (example)
    - Breakfast: protein source (egg/egg whites or yogurt), fiber (oats/berries), healthy fat (nuts or avocado).
    - Lunch: lean protein, vegetables, whole grain, healthy fat.
    - Snack: yogurt or cheese with fruit, or a protein shake with a small piece of fruit.
    - Dinner: lean protein, vegetables, moderate starch (sweet potato, quinoa) if training late.
    - Pre/post workout: small snack with protein + moderate carbs if training >60 minutes.

  MEDICATION CONSIDERATIONS
    - Continue metformin per clinician guidance.
    - If starting new exercise plan, monitor for GI effects and adjust timing of metformin if advised.
    - Watch for signs of hypoglycemia; adjust carbohydrate intake or dosing of medications as directed by healthcare provider.

  TESTING & PROGRESSION
    - Weekly check-ins: weight, waist circumference, energy level, sleep quality.
    - Every 4 weeks: adjust calories based on progress.
    - Reassess A1c and fasting glucose with clinician at 12 weeks; report results for program adjustments.

DIETARY RESTRICTIONS OR ALLERGIES
  - No known food allergies provided; substitute any item with equivalent macronutrient profile from standard options or discuss with client.

SAFETY NOTES
  - If client experiences any adverse symptoms (e.g., severe fatigue, chest pain, dizziness), pause exercise and contact clinician.
  - Avoid high-impact plyometrics or rapid loaded movements if joint pain or risk factors exist; substitute with controlled machine or resistance band alternatives.

END PLAN
